output.summary: The original request from SH-SUP was to build a chatbot so customers stop waiting for refund answers (CL-01). Analysis of authoritative payment-db and ticket-db data showed this framing was wrong: all 5 sampled refunds (R-0..R-4) fail execution with status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT (E-01), while ticket first-response time is already fast (2.0h median vs 24h SLA, 900 tickets, E-02). The problem was redefined (PD-1) as a backend IBAN-validation failure in process P-REF, supported by H-REFUND-IBAN-VALIDATION-FAILU (CONFIRMED) and H-BACKEND-REFUND-DELAY (SUPPORTED); the chatbot theory H-NO-SELFSERVICE-CHANNEL was REJECTED. The DEFINE gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring two HIGH-criticality unknowns (full-population IBAN failure rate; bank-api access impact) as open verification obligations. What was actually released was limited to verify_refund_ticket_consistency:DA-TCK (work items W-WI-1, W-WI-2, DONE) — confirming ticket/payment data consistency, not fixing the backlog or building the requested chatbot. The decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds, because the open VOBs block scope (measure_iban_failure_rate:DA-PAY, design_iban_validation_fix:P-REF) outside what was released, and bank-api is DEGRADED.
key_points: Initial request: build a chatbot for refund status answers, raised by SH-SUP (CL-01) and restated as CL-02/E-03.
Evidence E-01 (payment-db): all 5 sampled refunds R-0..R-4 fail with status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT, indicating a backend payout-execution failure.
Evidence E-02 (ticket-db): median first response time is 2.0h against a 24h SLA over 900 tickets, showing ticket communication is not the bottleneck.
Problem definition PD-1 (gate_result CONDITIONAL_PASS) concluded the root cause is IBAN-format validation failure in P-REF, not a missing fast-answer channel.

Hypotheses: H-REFUND-IBAN-VALIDATION-FAILU CONFIRMED and H-BACKEND-REFUND-DELAY SUPPORTED (both backed by E-01, E-02); H-NO-SELFSERVICE-CHANNEL (the chatbot theory) REJECTED, contradicted by E-01 and E-02.
Released scope was limited to verify_refund_ticket_consistency:DA-TCK (work items W-WI-1 and W-WI-2, DONE), per solution_design SD-1's minimum_useful_scope/release_scope.

Decision RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, hold list empty: two HIGH-impact verification obligations (VOB-U-FULL-POPULATION-RATE, VOB-U-BANKAPI-ACCESS-IMPACT) remain OPEN but their blocking_scope is outside the scope that was released.
Tool bank-api is DEGRADED, listed as a limitation affecting the unfinished work of correcting and resubmitting failed refunds.
limitations_explained: Unmeasured full-population IBAN failure rate: only the 5-record sample (R-0..R-4) was checked; VOB-U-FULL-POPULATION-RATE is open and the true failure rate across the full backlog is unknown.

Bank-api access impact unresolved: VOB-U-BANKAPI-ACCESS-IMPACT is open and bank-api tool health is DEGRADED, so it is unknown whether failed refunds can currently be resubmitted/corrected through the bank payout path.
The existing malformed-IBAN backlog (R-0..R-4 and the broader backlog) was not corrected or resubmitted in this release (SR-BACKLOG-IBAN-CORRECTION-RESU, feasible_in_contest_time: false).
A faster ticket-answer channel (the originally requested chatbot) would not address the backend root cause, since ticket response time is already within SLA per E-02.

U-TOOL-INTEGRATION-CONSISTENCY remains OPEN: whether a ticket-db/payment-db status mismatch (H-TOOL-INTEGRATION-FAILURE, CANDIDATE, no supporting evidence) independently contributes to repeat tickets is unresolved by this release's scope.
